description: Lunar Parametric Ops is an interdisciplinary team developing an interactive, AI-assisted parametric environment for lunar landing-site exploration. Combining NASA open data, computational geometry, spatial and temporal analysis, and human scientific verification, we aim to support collaborative exploration and informed decision-making.
summary:
At the lunar south pole, low solar elevations, varying Earth visibility, and rugged terrain make identifying promising landing-site candidates a spatial and temporal challenge. LUNAR-P/OPS is a research prototype for the Lunar Landing Site Navigator challenge, integrating NASA LOLA elevation data and SPICE geometry in an interactive parametric environment.
Its contributions include a dependency graph that generates immutable candidates from location, terrain, observer height, and time; an adaptive Region Brush that selects and refines locations using Sun/Earth visibility, slope, and roughness; and synchronized 3D terrain, graph, and timeline visualization. Stored evaluations preserve candidate lineage, scientific provenance, and reproducible results. An optional, read-only AI workflow interprets evidence without generating candidates or controlling calculations.
The architecture provides a foundation for transparent, locally executed exploration without requiring an LLM. Operation under constrained connectivity and energy efficiency, remain untested.
details:
At the lunar poles, low solar elevations, variable Earth visibility, and complex terrain complicate landing-site selection. LUNAR-P/OPS addresses this through an integrated parametric environment combining NASA data, scientific computations, adaptive exploration, and reproducible candidate evaluation.

Implemented Contributions

  • Parametric Candidate Graph: Connects location, terrain, observer height, and time to generate immutable, traceable candidates and revisions.
  • Adaptive Region Brush: Performs evidence-guided spatial exploration using solar/Earth visibility, terrain slope, roughness, and configurable constraints.
  • Integrated Visualization: Synchronizes 3D lunar terrain, dependency graphs, candidate information, and temporal evaluations.
  • Reproducibility: Preserves candidate lineage, scientific provenance, stored evaluations, and recomputation capabilities.
  • Optional AI Interpretation: A tested, read-only n8n workflow analyzes stored evidence without controlling candidate generation or scientific computations.

Future Research Potential

The implemented architecture provides a foundation for autonomous, locally executed lunar exploration under limited connectivity and constrained energy availability. Core operations function without an LLM, although autonomous deployment and energy efficiency have not yet been experimentally evaluated.
